notes.meaning: Saul was still full of hatred against the followers of Jesus, wanting to arrest or kill them. He went to the Jewish high priest in Jerusalem to get official support for his attacks. His fierce anger had become like the very air he breathed.

Saul asked for official letters to take to the Jewish meeting halls, called synagogues, in Damascus. These letters gave him permission to arrest any followers of Jesus, both men and women, and bring them back to Jerusalem as prisoners. Believers were known as followers of 'the Way' because they lived by following Jesus.

As Saul came near Damascus, a brilliant light from heaven suddenly flashed all around him. This was not ordinary sunlight, but the glorious presence of the risen Jesus shining down on him. God stopped this angry man in his tracks right before he reached the city.

Overwhelmed by the light, Saul fell flat on the ground and heard a voice speaking to him. The voice called his name twice and asked why he was attacking Him. Jesus made it clear that hurting believers is the same as hurting Jesus Himself, because Christians are united to Him.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine explained that because Christ and the church form one body, the Head cried out from heaven on behalf of His members on earth.

notes.meaning: Saul was confused and asked who was speaking to him from heaven. The voice answered plainly, 'I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.' In a single moment, Saul realized that the Jesus he thought was dead was alive and ruling in glory.

Jesus told Saul to stand up and enter Damascus, where he would receive further instructions. Even though Jesus spoke from heaven, He chose to guide Saul through another person in the city. God often leads us one step at a time instead of showing the whole journey at once.

The men traveling with Saul stood frozen in shock. They heard the sound of the voice, but they did not see anyone speaking. They knew something supernatural had happened, yet the full message was meant only for Saul.

Saul stood up from the ground, but when he opened his eyes, he could see nothing at all. The blinding glory of Jesus had taken away his physical sight. His companions had to take him by the hand and lead him into Damascus like a child.

For three days, Saul remained completely blind in Damascus and refused to eat or drink anything. He was deeply shaken and spent this quiet, dark time praying to God. True repentance means turning completely away from sin to the Lord.

A faithful believer named Ananias lived in Damascus, and the Lord Jesus spoke to him in a vision. When Jesus called his name, Ananias answered right away, saying, 'Here I am, Lord.' Ananias was an ordinary disciple, yet God chose him for a vital task.

The Lord told Ananias to go to a well-known street named Straight and look for Saul of Tarsus at the house of a man named Judas. Jesus explained that Saul was currently praying. God noticed Saul's heartfelt prayers and was already arranging the answer.

Jesus explained that Saul had already seen a vision of a man named Ananias coming to lay hands on him. This touch from Ananias would restore Saul's sight. God was working on both men at the same time to prepare them for this meeting.

Ananias hesitated and told the Lord that he had heard many reports about Saul. Believers who fled Jerusalem had told how much terrible harm Saul had done to God's holy people there. Ananias felt genuine fear because Saul had such a fierce reputation.

Ananias added that Saul had come to Damascus with legal authority from the leading Jewish priests to arrest all believers. Followers of Jesus were known as people who 'call on Your name,' which meant they prayed to Jesus as God. Ananias wondered why he should go anywhere near such a dangerous enemy.

The Lord ordered Ananias to go anyway, revealing that Saul was His chosen tool. Saul was appointed to carry the message of Jesus to non-Jewish nations, kings, and the people of Israel. God can take the greatest enemy of the faith and turn him into a leader for His kingdom.

The Lord also told Ananias that He would show Saul how much he would have to suffer for Jesus. Saul had brought suffering upon many believers, but now he would endure pain and hardship for the gospel. Saul's willingness to suffer would prove that his faith was real.

Ananias obeyed the Lord, entered the house, and laid his hands on Saul. He welcomed him warmly as 'Brother Saul' and explained that Jesus had sent him so Saul could see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit. Ananias treated his former enemy as a true brother in the faith.

differ.view: Saul was converted on the road but received the filling of the Holy Spirit three days later as a distinct experience for ministry.
Being filled with the Holy Spirit here refers to special power given for ministry rather than a separate second stage of salvation.

notes.meaning: Right away, something like crusty flakes or scales fell from Saul's eyes, and he could see again. He immediately got up and was baptized to publicly show his new faith in Christ. Baptism is an outward washing with water that marks a person as belonging to Jesus.

differ.view: Saul arose to be completely immersed in water, which shows that Christian baptism is always performed by full dipping.
Saul received new spiritual life and the removal of sins in baptism, where Christ works to cleanse the heart.
Saul's sins were already forgiven by faith, and baptism was an outward sign and seal confirming the grace God had already granted.

notes.meaning: Saul ate food and got his physical strength back after his three days of fasting. He then spent several days staying with the local believers in Damascus. The man who had come to jail these Christians was now living among them in peace and friendship.

Saul went straight into the Jewish meeting places and began preaching that Jesus is the Son of God. He did not wait or hesitate, but instantly declared what he had learned on the road. Knowing Christ creates a strong desire to tell others about Him.

Everyone who heard Saul was shocked and amazed. They remembered that he was the very man who had tried to destroy believers in Jerusalem and had traveled to Damascus to arrest them. A change this sudden showed the power of God at work.

Saul grew more and more capable in his speaking and baffled the Jewish leaders in Damascus. He laid Old Testament prophecies side by side with the life of Jesus to prove that Jesus is the promised Messiah, or Savior. God gave him great wisdom and spiritual power to defend the truth.
